items.title: 6.2.5 Intersection of a Line and a Circle (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 176-178: 6.2.5 line y = mx + c and circle x^2 + y^2 = a^2, discriminant Cases I-III, Corollary 1 (tangency), Corollary 2 (point of contact)

blocks.text: Ek seedhi line aur ek circle ko kaghaz par banaiye. Teen hi soorten mumkin hain: line circle ko do jagah kaate, sirf ek jagah chhoo kar guzar jaye, ya circle se door rahe. Is sabaq mein hum yahi teen soorten algebra se pehchanna seekhenge. Sab se aham nateeja beech wali soorat hai, kyun ke wahi tangent hai, aur us se ek bohat kaam ka formula nikalta hai: kisi diye hue slope wale tangents ki equation.

Maan lijiye line ki equation hai
\[y = mx + c \quad \text{...(1)}\]
aur circle ki equation hai
\[x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Intersection points (milne ke points) ke coordinates (1) aur (2) ke simultaneous solutions (dono ko ek saath poora karne wale jawab) hain. (1) se \(y\) ki value (2) mein rakhte hain:
\[x^{2} + (mx + c)^{2} = a^{2}\]
\((mx + c)^{2}\) ko \((a + b)^{2}\) wale formula se kholiye:
\[x^{2} + m^{2}x^{2} + 2mxc + c^{2} - a^{2} = 0\]
\(x^{2}\) wale terms ko ikattha kijiye:
\[x^{2}(1 + m^{2}) + 2mcx + (c^{2} - a^{2}) = 0 \quad \text{...(3)}\]
Equation (3) \(x\) mein quadratic hai aur \(x\) ki do values deti hai, maslan \(x_{1}\) aur \(x_{2}\). In ke mutabiq line se \(y_{1}\) aur \(y_{2}\) milte hain. Is tarah line \(y = mx + c\) circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) ko zyada se zyada do points \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) aur \((x_{2}, y_{2})\) par kaatti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Substitute kyun kiya? Intersection point line par bhi hai aur circle par bhi, is liye us ke coordinates dono equations ko ek hi waqt mein poora karte hain. \(y = mx + c\) ko circle mein rakhne se sirf \(x\) wali ek equation bach jati hai, jo hal karna aasan hai.
"Zyada se zyada do" kyun? Equation (3) quadratic hai (us ka pehla coefficient \(1 + m^{2}\) kabhi zero nahin hota, kyun ke \(m^{2} \ge 0\)), aur quadratic ke zyada se zyada do roots hote hain. Har real root \(x\) se ek point milta hai, jis ka \(y\) line se aata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yaad kijiye: \(Ax^{2} + Bx + C = 0\) ka discriminant \(B^{2} - 4AC\) hota hai. Yahan \(A = 1 + m^{2}\), \(B = 2mc\), \(C = c^{2} - a^{2}\). Discriminant positive ho to do alag real roots; zero ho to ek dohra root; negative ho to koi real root nahin. Yahi teen soorten neeche ke teen cases hain.
Case-I: Two distinct real points

Line \(y = mx + c\) aur circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) ke do intersection points real aur alag alag (distinct) hote hain agar discriminant \(> 0\) ho, yani agar
\[4[a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2}] > 0\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2} > 0\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) > c^{2}\]
Aisi line ko secant (kaatne wali line) kehte hain: circle mein ek taraf se dakhil hoti hai aur doosri taraf se nikal jati hai.
Case-II: One real point (tangent)

Line \(y = mx + c\) circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) ko sirf ek real point par chhooti hai, yani dono points mil kar ek ho jate hain (coincident points), agar discriminant \(= 0\) ho, yani agar
\[4[a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2}] = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2} = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) = c^{2}\]
Yahi tangent wala case hai, aur is sabaq ka sab se aham nateeja isi se nikalta hai.
Case-III: No real intersection

Line \(y = mx + c\) circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) ko do imaginary points par kaatti hai (yani asal mein circle ko kaatti hi nahin) agar discriminant \(< 0\) ho, yani agar
\[4[a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2}] < 0\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2} < 0\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) < c^{2}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
In teen cases ki ek saada tasveer hai. Centre \((0, 0)\) se line \(mx - y + c = 0\) ka faasla \(d = \frac{|c|}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\) hai. Is liye \(a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) \gtreqless c^{2}\) bilkul wahi baat hai jo \(a \gtreqless d\):
\(d < a\): line circle ke andar se guzarti hai aur do jagah kaatti hai (secant).
\(d = a\): line circle ko bas chhooti hai (tangent).
\(d > a\): line circle se door rehti hai.
Socho ek gol talaab hai aur ek seedhi sarak. Agar sarak ka centre se faasla talaab ke radius se kam hai to sarak talaab ke beech se guzregi; barabar ho to sirf kinare ko chhoo kar; zyada ho to talaab se door.
Corollary-1: Condition of Tangency of a Line to a Circle

Ab do nateeje (corollaries) nikalte hain. Corollary ka matlab hai woh baat jo kisi pichli baat se seedhi nikal aaye, bina kisi nayi mehnat ke. Pehla nateeja batata hai ke line kab tangent hoti hai; doosra batata hai ke woh circle ko kis point par chhooti hai.

Case II se: line \(y = mx + c\) circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) ka tangent hai agar:
\[|c| = a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}} \quad \text{ya} \quad c = \pm a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\]
Is liye circle ke tangents ki family (khandan: ek hi qisam ki saari lines) yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: y equals m x plus or minus a times the square root of 1 plus m squared

blocks.text:
Ghor kijiye ke \(\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\) centre \((0, 0)\) se line tak perpendicular faasla hai.
Is liye tangency ki shart yeh hai ke yeh faasla \(\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\) radius \(a\) ke barabar ho.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(y = mx \pm a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) ko kab aur kaise istemal karein? Jab tangent ka slope \(m\) maloom ho (maslan kisi di hui line ke parallel ya perpendicular ho, ya x-axis se koi angle banaye), to \(m\) aur radius \(a\) is formula mein rakh dein. \(\pm\) se do tangents milte hain, jo aapas mein parallel aur circle ke aamne saamne hote hain.
Yeh formula sirf us circle ke liye hai jis ka centre origin par ho. Kisi aur circle ke liye yahi idea seedha lagaiye: centre se line ka faasla = radius.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin. Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 9\) ke woh tangents nikaliye jin ka slope \(\frac{4}{3}\) ho. Yahan \(a = 3\), \(m = \frac{4}{3}\):
\[y = \dfrac{4}{3}x \pm 3\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{16}{9}}\]
\(\sqrt{1 + \frac{16}{9}} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{9}} = \frac{5}{3}\), is liye:
\[y = \dfrac{4}{3}x \pm 5\]
Tasdeeq: 3 se zarb dein to \(4x - 3y \pm 15 = 0\); origin se faasla \(\frac{15}{\sqrt{16 + 9}} = \frac{15}{5} = 3\), jo radius hai.
Corollary 2: Coordinates of Point of Contact

Tangent ki equation mil gayi, magar aksar sawal yeh bhi poochta hai ke tangent circle ko kahan chhoota hai. Is ka jawab bhi isi quadratic (3) mein chhupa hai: tangent ke case mein us ka sirf ek root hota hai, aur wahi point of contact ka \(x\)-coordinate hai.

Tangent \(y = mx + a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) ke liye quadratic equation (3) ke roots barabar hain (kyun ke \(D = 0\)), aur woh root yeh hai:
\[x = \dfrac{-2mc}{2(1 + m^{2})} = \dfrac{-mc}{1 + m^{2}}\]
Ab \(c = a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) rakhiye:
\[= \dfrac{-m}{1 + m^{2}}\left(a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{-am}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\]
(Neeche \(1 + m^{2} = \sqrt{1 + m^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) hai, us mein se ek \(\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) upar wale se cancel ho gaya.) Ab yeh \(x\) line \(y = mx + a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) mein rakhiye:
\[y = m\left(\dfrac{-am}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\right) + a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-am^{2}}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}} + a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\]
Common denominator \(\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) lein:
\[= \dfrac{-am^{2} + a(1 + m^{2})}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\]
\[= \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\]
Is tarah point of contact yeh hai:
\[\left(\dfrac{-am}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}, \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\right)\]
Isi tarah tangent \(y = mx - a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) ka point of contact:
\[\left(\dfrac{am}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}, \dfrac{-a}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\right)\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(x = \frac{-2mc}{2(1 + m^{2})}\) kyun? Jab discriminant zero ho to quadratic formula ka \(\pm\sqrt{D}\) wala hissa khatam ho jata hai aur sirf ek root bachta hai, \(x = -\frac{B}{2A}\).
Circle par tasdeeq: \(\frac{a^{2}m^{2}}{1 + m^{2}} + \frac{a^{2}}{1 + m^{2}} = \frac{a^{2}(m^{2} + 1)}{1 + m^{2}} = a^{2}\). Yani point waqai circle par hai.
Dono points of contact ek doosre ke ulte (negative) hain, yani ek hi diameter ke do sire. Yeh samajh mein aata hai: do parallel tangents circle ke bilkul aamne saamne chhoote hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Line \(y = x + 5\) aur circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 9\): kya line circle ko kaatti hai? (Ishara: \(a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) = 9 \times 2 = 18\) aur \(c^{2} = 25\). \(18 < 25\), is liye Case-III: line circle ko nahin kaatti.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Line aur circle ka milap dhoondna ho to line ko circle mein rakh kar quadratic hal kijiye.
2. \(y = mx + c\) aur \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) ke liye \(D = 4[a^{2}(1 + m^{2}) - c^{2}]\).
3. \(D > 0\): do points; \(D = 0\): tangent; \(D < 0\): koi real point nahin.
4. Tangency: \(c^{2} = a^{2}(1 + m^{2})\); slope \(m\) wale tangents: \(y = mx \pm a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\).
5. \(y = mx + a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) ka point of contact: \(\left(\frac{-am}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}, \frac{a}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\right)\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(c = \pm a\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}\) aise circle par laga dena jis ka centre origin par nahin.
2. Line \(y = mx + c\) wale \(c\) ko general circle wale constant \(c\) se mila dena; is sabaq mein circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\) hai.
3. \(\pm\) chhor dena: diye hue slope ke do tangents hote hain.
4. Point of contact ulta jor dena: \(+\) wale tangent ka \(y\)-coordinate \(+\frac{a}{\sqrt{1 + m^{2}}}\) hai.
